author_role: independent held-out fault author; not executor or outcome scorer

fault_label_policy.label: historical-pattern-inspired independently authored held-out mutations
fault_label_policy.reason: The mutations instantiate reported serving failure patterns on the fixed ForkAudit stack; they do not run the upstream servers, allocators, offload connectors, or sliding-window paths from those reports.

fixed_stack.hardware: three distinct NVIDIA H20-3e devices drawn from the existing eight-device node
fixed_stack.software: the same pinned Torch 2.11.0+cu129 / Transformers 5.14.1 / vLLM 0.26 environment as R28
fixed_stack.execution_scope: fresh sequential disposable cases; this workstream is not the separate concurrency experiment

lanes.purpose: measure what completion, production assertions, token equality, and full-logit equality reveal without using receipt verdicts
apply the same fault and the same advertised horizon, then run the uniform receipt battery

faults.class: prefix-cache identity/content mismatch after a non-append history change
faults.frozen_intervention: For request 0 at the first full-attention layer, exchange immutable document-page entries 1 and 2 in the request-local live block table. Do not change pool bytes, table geometry, dtype/device, request identity, reservations, or any other layer.
faults.injection_stage: after fresh resident construction and before the one-token model invocation
faults.guaranteed_target_symptom: the request-local route order no longer represents the frozen prefix while every basic tensor-shape and dtype/device check remains valid
faults.external_symptom_hypothesis: the model may complete but its deterministic full logits or token may differ from the clean prefix; this is measured, not required for scientific validity

source_provenance.title: Token truncation leaves stale Request.block_hashes and can cause incorrect KV cache hits
source_provenance.pattern_used: a live token history changes non-append-only while its reusable prefix identity remains stale
a reusable block identity must bind parent prefix, exact block tokens, and relevant extra hashes

faults.transfer_limit: The fixed stack has no vLLM V1 Request.block_hashes lookup in this case; H01 injects the reported consequence at the live page-routing boundary and is not an exact reproduction of issue 49377.
faults.restoration_policy: restore both selected route entries exactly; require restored descriptor SHA-256 to equal pre-intervention SHA-256

faults.frozen_intervention: Run the same frozen one-token input twice for request 0 without rewinding recurrent state, while the advertised logical history advances by only one token. The second invocation is a hidden resume retry of the already-applied boundary token.
faults.injection_stage: model action sequence at an advertised one-token resume boundary
faults.guaranteed_target_symptom: actual model invocations equal two while the externally advertised logical advance equals one and both invocations use the identical frozen token coordinate
faults.external_symptom_hypothesis: the model is expected to complete and may return different deterministic full logits or token at the advertised history; divergence is measured rather than assumed

source_provenance.title: OffloadingConnector can silently return wrong output at exact chunk boundaries with mamba_cache_mode=all
source_provenance.pattern_used: restored recurrent state already contains boundary token N while the scheduler recomputes N

faults.transfer_limit: The fixed stack does not enable the upstream OffloadingConnector or Mamba cache mode. H02 recreates only the double-apply consequence on GDN state and is not an exact reproduction of issue 51094.
faults.restoration_policy: no in-place target restoration; every lane uses a fresh disposable cache/model case and the action-sequence receipt is immutable

faults.class: allocator ownership becomes stale before the bad route is consumed
faults.frozen_intervention: For request 0 at the first full-attention layer, replace only private reservation index 1 with request 1's corresponding physical block id. Preserve reservation index 0. With a 4095-token prefix and one appended token, index 1 must remain inactive over the measured horizon.
faults.injection_stage: after fresh resident construction and before the one-token model invocation
faults.guaranteed_target_symptom: one future reservation is multiply owned but remains outside the active block table for the preregistered one-token horizon
faults.external_symptom_hypothesis: clean and faulty tokens/full logits are expected to remain exact through the short horizon because the bad future reservation is not consumed; equality is measured and a divergence does not invalidate the run

source_provenance.title: SWA eviction leaves stale block table entries
source_provenance.pattern_used: a freed or reusable physical block id can remain reachable in stale worker/GPU routing metadata while current masking keeps it semantically inactive

source_provenance.title: Potential use-after-free in KV block allocator under eviction pressure
source_provenance.pattern_used: a physical block owned by another request can bleed into a victim after allocator reuse

faults.transfer_limit: The fixed stack does not run sliding-window eviction or vLLM's production block allocator. H03 is a latent consequence-level reservation fault, not a reproduction or confirmation of either upstream report.
faults.restoration_policy: restore the single future reservation exactly; require restored descriptor SHA-256 to equal pre-intervention SHA-256

checks: fault target precondition and non-no-op intervention receipt
unchanged target tensor rank, shape, stride, dtype, and device
model invocation completion versus an exact allowlisted production assertion
greedy token equality against the matched clean advertised horizon
full FP32 logit byte-SHA equality, max-absolute difference, and relative-L2 against the matched clean advertised horizon

ordered_checks: live KV ownership and construction binding after the advertised horizon
GDN phase/storage snapshot and pointer-free replay after the advertised horizon
persistent KV and GDN immutability guards
mutation restoration or fresh-case disposal receipt
uniform_forkaudit_receipt_battery.classification_rule: A ForkAudit catch requires an authenticated receipt predicate rejection or replay rejection from the registered audit modules. No fault has a preregistered target detector, and an arbitrary exception never counts.

token_only.evaluated_only_if: clean and faulty lanes both reach the preregistered advertised semantic horizon

full_logit.evaluated_only_if: clean and faulty lanes both persist finite FP32 logits with shape [1,248320] at the advertised semantic horizon
